title: Ottawa launches new national AI council to advise on safety, deployment
key_facts: A Prime Minister's Office news release on Friday (2 Oct 2026) announced the Prime Minister's National Council on Artificial Intelligence.
The council is meant to convene public and private stakeholders and advise on the evolution of Canada's AI strategy.
Its advice covers speeding up AI adoption, building national champions in the industry, building AI infrastructure, making AI safer, protecting Canadian democracy and making sure Canadians benefit.

Named members include Yoshua Bengio (his company LawZero received $150 million in federal funding last month), Valerie Pisano (CEO of Mila), Sen. Tom Pitfield and Patrick Pichette (CEO of Digital Transformation Canada).
Pichette is also a member of Canada's AI strategy task force.
Carney said the council will inform and advise the government on how to deploy AI in Canada.
quote_evidence: "The new National Council on Artificial Intelligence will inform and advise the government on how to most effectively deploy AI in Canada — how to manage the risks, seize the opportunities and ensure AI is used to improve the lives of all Canadians," Prime Minister Mark Carney said in a statement.
Prime Minister Mark Carney has a new national council on artificial intelligence meant to provide the government with guidance for its AI strategy and on making the technology safer.
why_it_matters_hint: Canada now has a standing advisory group on AI strategy and safety, though the article gives no powers, budget or start date.
